explanation: W = 1.5929 GeV is above the ep -> e'p(eta) threshold (m_p + m_eta = 1.4861 GeV), so the point is physically accessible. The exclurad executable hardcodes 'open(unit=5,file="input.dat")' and ignores stdin redirection, so eta/my_input.dat's content (model=3 EtaMAID, rc_mode=0 full O(alpha), bmom=6.53 GeV, ivec=1 proton, vcut=0.166 GeV^2, single point W=1.5929, Q2=0.4276, cos(theta*)=0.651724, phi*=36 deg) was placed into eta/input.dat before running ./build/exclurad, then eta/input.dat was restored to its original 3-point template afterward. Results were read from eta/radtot.dat, which reports full double-precision values: delta = sigma_observed/sigma_Born (unpolarized, isf1=1..4) = 1.1413042153, and sigma_Born (sibar(1)) = 0.0055907670 (code-internal cross-section units, nb per the EXCLURAD/barn=.389379d6 GeV^-2->nb normalization). These match the truncated values in eta/radcor.dat (1.141) and eta/radsigpl.dat, confirming a converged, well-behaved calculation (integration test ratio 0.559E-02/0.559E-02 = 1.00).
